title: Etale ring maps: the conormal map of a finite presentation is an isomorphism
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $n\ge0$, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring, and $\alpha:P\to S$ a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras whose kernel $J$ is a finitely generated ideal of $P$. The quotient $J/J^2$ is an $S=P/J$-module, and let $\bigoplus_{k=1}^nS\,\mathrm dx_k$ be the free $S$-module on symbols $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$. The map $\mathrm d:J/J^2\to\bigoplus_{k=1}^nS\,\mathrm dx_k$, $\mathrm d(g\bmod J^2)=\sum_{k=1}^n\alpha(\partial g/\partial x_k)\,\mathrm dx_k$ ($\partial/\partial x_k$ the formal partial derivatives of $P$ over $R$), is well defined and $S$-linear. Then the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ induced by $R\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] if and only if $\mathrm d$ is bijective.

source.place: Definition Tag 00U1 (definition-etale, line 39245: $R\to S$ etale iff of finite presentation and $\NL_{S/R}$ quasi-isomorphic to zero, i.e. $H_1(\NL_{S/R})=0$ and $\Omega_{S/R}=0$), with the complex $\NL(\alpha):I/I^2\to\bigoplus S\,\mathrm dx_i$ of a presentation (text before Lemma Tag 00S1, line ~35190) and Lemma Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy, line 35274: $\NL(\alpha)\to\NL_{S/R}$ is a quasi-isomorphism); the cokernel of $\mathrm d$ is $\Omega_{S/R}$ by Lemma Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq); the comparison with etale morphisms of schemes by literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex Lemma Tag 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize) and the remark in def-weil-etale-morphism (Stacks 02GI, 02GV, 02GE). This is the form of etaleness used in the proof of Algebra Lemma Tag 07RI ('The assumption is that the map d ... is an isomorphism').

proof.text: Set P = MvPolynomial (Fin n) R and give S its P-algebra structure using alpha. Transport the quotient action on J.Cotangent along e.symm. The identity e.symm(alpha(p)) = mk J p gives IsScalarTower P S J.Cotangent. Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor constructs the P-linear conormal map c and LinearMap.extendScalarsOfSurjective makes it S-linear without changing its underlying function.

Use KaehlerDifferential.mvPolynomialBasis and its scalar extension b to identify S tensor Omega[P/R] with Fin n -> S via b.repr and Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite. Set d = t composed with c. The definition of c on toCotangent, Basis.baseChange_repr_tmul, and mvPolynomialBasis_repr_apply give d(g mod J^2)(i) = alpha(pderiv i g).

P is formally smooth by the polynomial instance. Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth.kerCotangentToTensor_injective_iff h_alpha identifies injectivity of c with Subsingleton (H1Cotangent R S), directly using presentation independence rather than the project Jacobi-Zariski quotient sequence. Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange and mapBaseChange_surjective give surjectivity of c iff Subsingleton Omega[S/R]: in the forward direction every differential is w(c(a)) = 0; in the reverse direction w(x) = 0 so exactness gives a preimage of x under c.

The finite presentation instance is supplied directly by n, alpha, h_alpha and h_fg. Apply HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff, RingHom.etale_algebraMap, Algebra.etale_iff and Algebra.formallyEtale_iff. Since t is a linear equivalence, d is bijective iff c is bijective. Substitute the two preceding equivalences and rearrange the conjunction to conclude.

lean.statement: theorem etale_ring_map_conormal_criterion {R : Type u} {S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] S) (hα : Function.Surjective α) (hfg : (RingHom.ker α.toRingHom).FG) : let J := RingHom.ker α.toRingHom let e := RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective hα letI : Module S J.Cotangent := Module.compHom J.Cotangent e.symm.toRingHom ∃ d : J.Cotangent →ₗ[S] (Fin n → S), (∀ (g : J) (i : Fin n), d (Ideal.toCotangent J g) i = α (MvPolynomial.pderiv i g.1)) ∧ (AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S))) ↔ Function.Bijective d)
